prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for TCS (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 221000,
      "net_income_cr": 43500,
      "eps": 119.0
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 247500,
      "net_income_cr": 48200,
      "eps": 132.5
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 272000,
      "net_income_cr": 52800,
      "eps": 145.5
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Revenue growth normalises toward a 15% blended rate in FY2023, reflecting the strong FY2022 rebound (16.8% YoY consolidated) driven by post-pandemic demand surge and broad-based deal wins across BFSI, Retail, CMT and Life Sciences, but mean-reverting slightly as the base effect diminishes; the 5-year CAGR implied by the 10-year highlights table (Total Revenue % growth: 19.0, 4.4, 8.6, 14.8, 15.7 for FY2019-FY2022 inclusive) supports a sustainable mid-teens growth trajectory, which is then moderated to ~12% by FY2025 as global macro headwinds (inflation, rate hikes, client discretionary spending caution) temper demand.",
    "Net profit margin is held broadly stable at ~22-22.5% of consolidated revenues (FY2022 PAT margin: 38,449/191,754 = 20.1% on consolidated basis; net profit ratio standalone 23.8%), with modest pressure from wage inflation and talent competition offset by operating leverage on higher revenues and continued efficiency in sub-contracting; the debt-free balance sheet (Debt/Equity = 0.0x across all years in the 10-year table) and strong free cash flow conversion (~92.6% of operating cash flow) provide ample capacity to sustain investments without dilutive financing."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2022 consolidated revenue grew 16.8% YoY (191,754 cr vs 164,177 cr) which is anomalously high relative to the prior two years (4.4% and 8.6%) but consistent with a post-pandemic demand recovery bounce; the 5-year revenue CAGR blends to approximately 14-15%, which is used as the forward anchor. FY2023 is projected at ~15% growth (~221,000 cr) capturing continued strong deal momentum and cloud/digital spending; growth tapers to ~12% in FY2024-25 as the high base effect and macro uncertainty (rising interest rates, possible client budget cuts in the Americas and Europe) create headwinds. Net income is forecast at ~19.7-19.4% of revenue, reflecting modest margin compression from continued talent investment and wage inflation, partially offset by operating leverage; EPS reflects a slightly declining share count due to ongoing buybacks (shares fell from 374 cr to 369.9 cr weighted average in FY2022)."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
